title: Correct user voltage (no transformer)
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the user voltage as 140 V, accounting for line loss.

title: Correct user power (no transformer)
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the user power as 28000 W, accounting for line loss.

title: Correct user voltage (with transformers)
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the user voltage as 219.2 V after step-down transformation.

title: Correct user power (with transformers)
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the user power as 43840 W after step-down transformation.

title: Apply transformer voltage ratio
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the transformer turns ratio to find stepped-up and stepped-down voltages.

title: Calculate line current correctly
description: Important: The student must correctly compute the transmission line current from power and voltage, both with and without transformers.

title: Account for line losses
description: Important: The student must compute voltage and power losses on the transmission line using Ohm's Law and P=I²R.

title: Power conservation in ideal transformers
description: Optional: The student may explicitly state that power is conserved through ideal transformers.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student's work should maintain consistent units (V, A, W, Ω) throughout.

title: Confuse voltage and power ratios
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly applies transformer ratios to power or confuses step-up/step-down ratios.

title: Neglect line losses
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student fails to subtract voltage or power losses when computing user values.

title: Incorrect current calculation
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses the wrong voltage (e.g., user voltage) to compute transmission line current.
